spatial_claims.claim: ABCD is a square: AB = BC = CD = DA, all angles are right angles
E is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD, so E lies on both diagonals
AB is parallel to DC (co-interior angles DAB + ADC = two right angles)
AD is parallel to BC (co-interior angles DAB + ABC = two right angles)
Alternate angles EAB = ECD with AB || DC and transversal AC
Alternate angles EBA = EDC with AB || DC and transversal BD
Triangle AEB congruent to triangle CED (ASA), giving EA = EC and EB = ED
Triangle ABD is isosceles with DA = AB
Angle ADB = angle ABD = half a right angle
Triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = BC
Angle BAC = angle BCA = half a right angle
In triangle AEB, angle EAB = angle BAC (ray AE = ray AC since E is on AC)
In triangle AEB, angle EBA = angle ABD (ray BE = ray BD since E is on BD)
EA = EB since triangle AEB is isosceles (equal base angles)
EA = EB = EC = ED (E is equidistant from all four vertices)
Circle with center E and radius EA passes through A, B, C, D

configuration_map: Point E: Constructed as intersection of diagonals AC and BD of square ABCD. E lies between A and C on diagonal AC, and between B and D on diagonal BD. Because E is interior to the square and on both diagonals, ray AE coincides with ray AC, and ray BE coincides with ray BD. Triangle AEB is formed by adjacent vertices A, B and center E, with angles of 45-45-90 degrees. The configuration is fully consistent: E is the center of the square, equidistant from all four vertices.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The key identifications (ray AE = ray AC, ray BE = ray BD) are valid because E lies between the endpoints of each diagonal. The parallel-line alternate-angle arguments are correctly applied. The ASA congruence correctly establishes EA = EC and EB = ED, and the isosceles triangle argument correctly establishes EA = EB. The proof takes a different but geometrically sound path from Heath's.
